findings.title: Unsanitized LLM output rendered as HTML via v-html
findings.description: AI-generated weekly report content is rendered using Vue's v-html directive without any sanitization. The renderedContent computed property converts markdown-like LLM output to HTML and injects it directly into the DOM.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1. Attacker manipulates the LLM (via prompt injection on the LLM provider side, or by compromising the LLM API response) to include malicious HTML/JS in the report content. 2. When the user opens the Weekly Report panel, the malicious payload executes in the renderer process via v-html. 3. This bypasses Vue's default HTML escaping and enables XSS. In Electron, while contextIsolation is enabled, XSS in the renderer can still be used for phishing UI, data exfiltration via IPC calls (through the exposed window.matrixflow API), or potentially chaining with other renderer vulnerabilities.
findings.impact: Cross-site scripting in renderer process. Malicious scripts can interact with the exposed MatrixFlow API (window.matrixflow), trigger IPC calls, manipulate UI to trick users, or exfiltrate data.
findings.recommendation: Replace v-html with a sanitized HTML renderer (e.g., DOMPurify) or use a safe markdown-to-HTML library that sanitizes output. Alternatively, render the report as plain text or use Vue components instead of raw HTML injection.

findings.title: HIGH severity vulnerability in electron-builder dependency tree (tar)
findings.description: npm audit identified HIGH severity vulnerabilities in the electron-builder dependency tree, specifically app-builder-lib and dmg-builder, caused by a vulnerable tar package. CVSS indicates local attack vector with availability impact.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1. An attacker with local access or via a compromised dependency could exploit the tar vulnerability during the build process. 2. This is primarily a build-time risk; the vulnerable code is in devDependencies used for packaging, not in the runtime application.
findings.impact: Build-time supply chain risk. Could affect the integrity of packaged Electron applications if the build environment is compromised.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade electron-builder to version 26.8.1 or later, which resolves these vulnerabilities. Note: this is a semver-major upgrade, so test builds thoroughly after updating.

findings.title: Remote selector YAML fetched without signature verification
findings.description: SelectorUpdateService fetches platform selector configurations (YAML) from a remote URL (default: raw.githubusercontent.com) and parses them without any cryptographic signature verification, checksum validation, or TLS certificate pinning. The parsed selectors directly control Patchright browser automation behavior (which elements to click, type, etc.).
findings.exploit_scenario: 1. Attacker compromises the GitHub repository hosting the selectors, performs a MITM attack on the network path, or poisons DNS to serve a malicious YAML file. 2. MatrixFlow downloads and applies the malicious selectors. 3. The malicious selectors instruct Patchright to navigate to attacker-controlled pages, enter credentials into wrong fields, or exfiltrate session cookies/platform tokens during the automated login/publish flow.
findings.impact: Complete compromise of platform account credentials and session tokens. Malicious selectors could redirect login flows to phishing pages or exfiltrate cookies during automated publishing.
findings.recommendation: Implement signature verification for remote selector updates (e.g., sign YAML with an Ed25519 key embedded in the application, verify before applying). Alternatively, pin a known-good hash for each selector file and verify the downloaded content matches. At minimum, implement a content-type check and schema validation before applying selectors.

findings.title: Third-party GitHub Action not SHA-pinned
findings.description: The workflow uses softprops/action-gh-release@v2, a third-party action, pinned only to a major version tag rather than a specific commit SHA. Tags can be force-moved by the action maintainer or compromised to deliver malicious code.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1. The softprops/action-gh-release repository is compromised (maintainer account takeover, supply chain attack). 2. The attacker force-pushes the v2 tag to a malicious commit. 3. The next MatrixFlow release build executes the malicious action, which has access to GITHUB_TOKEN and could modify releases, exfiltrate signing certificates, or inject malicious artifacts.
findings.impact: Supply chain compromise of release artifacts. Malicious action could steal signing certificates, tamper with release binaries, or exfiltrate repository secrets.
findings.recommendation: Pin the action to a specific commit SHA (e.g., softprops/action-gh-release@c9b46fe7aad9a04e6c660ea8c8c8cf5e1d5437f8) instead of a version tag. Verify the SHA against the action's official release notes.

findings.title: Missing CODEOWNERS file for workflow protection
findings.description: No CODEOWNERS file exists in the repository. The GitHub Actions workflow file (build.yml) is not protected by required reviews from specific maintainers, allowing any contributor with write access to modify the workflow and potentially exfiltrate secrets or compromise the build pipeline.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1. A compromised contributor account or malicious PR modifies .github/workflows/build.yml to add a step that exfiltrates secrets (CSC_LINK, CSC_KEY_PASSWORD, APPLE_ID_PASSWORD) to an external server. 2. Without CODEOWNERS requiring review from a specific trusted maintainer, the PR could be merged and executed.
findings.impact: Unauthorized modification of CI/CD pipeline leading to secret exfiltration or build artifact tampering.
findings.recommendation: Create a CODEOWNERS file at the repository root with a rule like `.github/workflows/ @trusted-maintainer` to require review from designated maintainers for any workflow changes.
